item.title: South Africa cautions Fani-Kayode over social media remarks
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye South Africa has cautioned Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, over his social media remarks following the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa. The country’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation, DIRCO, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, following a meeting between its Director-General, Zane Dangor, and Fani-Kayode. According to the statement, Dangor conveyed South Africa’s concerns over the events that followed the presentation of the Nigerian envoy’s Letters of Credence to Ramaphosa, as well as his subsequent comments on social media. The statement said, “During the meeting, the Director-General conveyed South Africa’s concern regarding events that transpired following the presentation of the High Commissioner’s Letters of Credence to His Excellency President Cyril Ramaphosa, as well as subsequent remarks made on social media.” Dangor also recalled Article 41 of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which requires diplomatic agents to conduct official business with the receiving country through its Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The statement added, “Mr Dangor further recalled the provisions of Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961), which require diplomatic agents to conduct official business with the receiving State through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. “In this regard, it was emphasised that all official communication should be conducted through established diplomatic channels, including DIRCO.” The South African department further reaffirmed the importance of preserving the longstanding bilateral relationship between both countries, founded on mutual respect, friendship and cooperation. It said, “South Africa remains committed to the continued strengthening of its strategic partnership with Nigeria and to maintaining constructive diplomatic engagement in the spirit of African solidarity and mutual respect.” Background The development follows a diplomatic controversy that erupted after Fani-Kayode presented his Letters of Credence to Ramaphosa at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria on November 13, alongside ambassadors from 14 other countries. The former minister of aviation had accused the South African presidency of deliberately excluding his introduction and speech from the official livestream of the ceremony, alleging that the broadcast cut off around the time he was scheduled to speak and resumed only after his address. In a post on his X handle, Fani-Kayode said he was the only ambassador whose introduction and speech were omitted from the broadcast, describing the development as deliberate. He also claimed that he raised the matter with Ramaphosa during a photo session after the ceremony, adding that the South African President directed relevant officials to address his complaint. item.title: Radda Warns Against ‘419 Politicians’ As Supporters Rally For APC In Katsina
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has urged voters to reject what he described as “419 politicians” in the 2027 general elections, declaring that only leaders with proven records of service deserve the people’s mandate. The governor appealed on Tuesday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally at the Mai’adua International Border Market in Mai’adua Local Government Area, where thousands of APC supporters gathered as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone. Addressing the enthusiastic crowd, Governor Radda said the massive turnout reflected public confidence in his administration’s performance, particularly in healthcare delivery, education, teacher recruitment, youth empowerment and other development programmes. Supporters rally for Tinubu in Katsina State. He expressed appreciation to the people of Mai’adua for their overwhelming support and pledged to consolidate on the achievements of his administration if re-elected. “We have nothing to say but to thank God for the people of Mai’adua. We are grateful for the support we have received from women, youths and the elderly. This massive turnout shows that the people are satisfied with our achievements and leadership, especially in healthcare, education, teacher recruitment and empowerment.» “Please don’t make the mistake of electing 419 politicians. I know you are not in support of such politicians, and by the grace of God, we will reciprocate this confidence if re-elected. You have also demonstrated that you are genuine supporters and true admirers of the late President Muhammadu Buhari.” The governor also welcomed thousands of defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) into the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the development as further evidence of the ruling party’s growing popularity across the state. The rally’s highlight was the presentation of an Award of Excellence to Governor Radda by health workers in Mai’adua Local Government Area in recognition of what they described as his transformative leadership and commitment to strengthening the state’s healthcare sector. Earlier, Governor Radda commissioned the newly constructed Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) Dumurkul Division in Mai’adua Local Government Area. The security facility was built by the Chairman of Mai’adua Local Government, Hon. Mamman Salisu Na-Allahu, as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots security and enhance the fight against insecurity in the border communities. Commissioning the project, Governor Radda commended the council chairman for his foresight and commitment to safeguarding lives and property, stressing that security remains the cornerstone of his administration’s development agenda. He charged officers of the NSCDC to uphold professionalism, diligence, and discipline in the discharge of their duties while fostering stronger collaboration with other security agencies and host communities. item.title: Senate chief whip, Monguno, others escape suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Senate Chief Whip and Senator representing Borno North, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, alongside some All Progressives Congress (APC) stalwarts, have escaped Boko Haram’s attempted attack in the Kukawa Local Government Area of the state. Sources said Monguno and a former Governor Senator Maina Maaji Lawan, among others, stormed Kukawa in continuation of their 2027 campaign tour. Earlier, Monguno had joined Governor Babagana Zulum at the official launch of the campaign in Monguno town last Sunday, before the governor disengaged on Monday from Monguno back to Maiduguri via a helicopter, while some of his entourage arrived in Maiduguri the same day by road. Sources said some politicians, including the Senate Chief Whip, proceeded from Monguno to Kukawa to canvass for votes, in which the terrorists attempted to dislodge the community. It was also gathered that, based on intelligence, troops of Operation Hadin Kai swung into action and foiled the attempted attacks by terrorists on the campaign entourage. According to reports by Yerwa News Express, a local online media outlet said, “The terrorists fired three mortar bombs toward Kukawa on Monday while Mr Monguno, former Borno State Governor Maina Maaji Lawan, and other political figures were in the town for campaign activities. “Local sources had earlier reported threats by the terrorists to disrupt the campaign, prompting heightened security measures. “Troops of Operation Hadin Kai detected the movement of the terrorists around Kukawa and swiftly responded, preventing them from carrying out the attack. “The campaign team subsequently returned safely to Monguno without any casualties. “The terrorists reportedly made further attempts to attack the town throughout the night but were prevented from gaining access.” In a related development, troops foiled another attempted attack on Kekeno village in the early hours of Tuesday, November 17, 2026. “At about 1:20 a.m., alert troops spotted suspicious movements by suspected terrorists travelling on foot from the general area of Barwati toward Kekeno village. “The troops immediately advanced toward the suspected terrorists and engaged them with heavy gunfire. “Unable to withstand the troops’ firepower, the terrorists reportedly fled into the surrounding bush. “The military said follow-up operations are ongoing in the area to track down the fleeing terrorists. “It added that the situation remained calm, with troops maintaining heightened surveillance.” Sources and Yerwa Express News reported. Due to a lack of telecommunication networks in the zone, the Senate Chief Whip’s phone number was not available at the time our correspondent dialled to confirm the incident. item.title: Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased. Atiku, in a condolence message on his X handle on Tuesday, expressed sadness over Ajasa’s death at the age of 44, saying his passing was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short. He wrote, “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed. “His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.” Atiku also extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and everyone who knew and worked with the late journalist. “I extend my heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, Editor Eze Anaba, and all who loved and worked with him,” the statement added. “May the memories they shared bring comfort in this difficult hour, and may God grant his family strength to bear this immeasurable loss. “May his soul rest in peace.” Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness. He was aged 44, according to a statement by the management of Vanguard Media Limited. His death has continued to attract tributes from political figures, media practitioners and other Nigerians, who have mourned his passing and remembered his contributions to journalism. The post Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ₦70,000 Transport Controversy: FG Constitutes Committee To Review New Minimum Wages For Workers
item.description: The Federal Government has approved the constitution of a new committee to comprehensively examine and address the issues raised by the Trade Union Congress (TUC) regarding a new minimum wage for Nigerian workers. The development was revealed by the TUC’s Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, in a statement on Tuesday, following a meeting with the Federal Government in response to a letter dated 8th October, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the Union. TUC President, Alex Osifo, in handshake with Ayo Fayose during the meeting While the meeting was chaired by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, the TUC delegation was led by the President, Comrade Engr. Festus Osifo, and comprised Comrade General N.A. Toro, Secretary-General; Comrade Shehu Mohammed, Deputy President; Comrade Akintola Benjamin, Trustee; and Comrade Kamal Ibrahim, Auditor II. Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, during the meeting Also in attendance were the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana. While providing further explanation, TUC noted that it had insisted on a salary increment rather than a mere one-off N70,000 six-month transportation package. “In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage. “This position, alongside the other demands and concerns raised by Congress, will form part of the issues to be thoroughly interrogated by the High-Powered Committee”, the statement read in part. According to the statement, the government has already attended to some of the demands raised by the TUC. “The Committee will therefore undertake a comprehensive review and reconciliation of the issues, establish the extent of actions already taken by the Government, identify outstanding matters and make appropriate findings and recommendations”, the statement said in part. The composition of the High-Powered Committee includes three representatives from the TUC, led by the Secretary-General, Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (OSGF), Permanent Secretary, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF), National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment. The High-Powered Committee is expected to commence work immediately and submit its report to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation within two weeks. item.title: ‘Nigeria is finished’ narrative costing economy investments, jobs — FG
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigeria is paying a heavy economic price for negative narratives, misinformation and damaging perceptions about the country. Negative stories, he said, are not merely public relations problems. They discourage investors, constrain businesses, and drive away skilled talent. Oyedele spoke at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja on Tuesday. He identified public trust as a critical factor in attracting investment, sustaining businesses and securing citizens’ support for government policies. According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand. Oyedele said, “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.” The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives are often overlooked. The country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness. He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished”, “Nigeria is a scam”, and “Nigeria happened to me”, warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects. Oyedele further explained that the cost went beyond reputational damage. Investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, businesses postpone expansion plans, and talented Nigerians seek opportunities elsewhere. He, however, acknowledged that citizens have the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism. The country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress, he added. Government and businesses could not rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. “We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said. Oyedele stressed that public communication must be backed by measurable results. Citizens judged government not by announcements or budgetary provisions but by what they experienced. The minister noted that the disconnect between government claims and citizens’ everyday experiences had contributed to distrust, making it difficult for even well-intentioned policies to gain public acceptance. He used the public’s response to declining inflation figures to illustrate the challenge. item.title: British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway
item.description: By Dickson Omobola British Airways Flight BA75 from Heathrow, London, to Lagos, Nigeria, veered off the runway shortly before take-off today. The aircraft, which had up to 215 passengers on board, was subsequently grounded, resulting in the cancellation of the flight. Pictures shared with The Sun showed the Boeing 787 Dreamliner stranded, with its nose wheel stuck in a grass verge. According to The Sun, emergency services raced to the scene of the stranded aircraft, which had sparked disruption at the airport. Airport sources suggested to The Sun that pilot error could have been responsible for the incident, which occurred at about 10.40am. A source told The Sun, “The packed plane was all set to go and had pushed back from its stand, taxiing to the runway for take-off to Lagos. “Bafflingly, the plane appears to have simply been driven off the tarmac onto a grass verge. It is hard to understand what could be to blame for this, other than a most basic pilot error. “There are red faces all around the airline, and a hefty task clearing up the mess and looking after hundreds of disgruntled passengers who were strapped in their seats for lift-off.” British Airways told The Sun, “We are very sorry to our customers for the disruption to their flight. Our teams are working to get them on their way as quickly as possible and are in touch with them to put things right.” The post British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Vinicius hits 12-minute hat-trick as Brazil thrash Singapore 7-0
item.description: Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore on Tuesday. Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also scored as the South Americans brushed aside the hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium. Brazil were much changed from their 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday in which manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were shown red cards, with Vinicius one of only four players retaining their places in the starting line-up. Bruno Guimaraes took over as skipper and set up the opener after nine minutes, playing a quick pass to Vinicius who wrong-footed Singapore captain Hariss Harun with his first touch before despatching a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud. The Real Madrid forward notched his second in the 15th minute after a quick counter-attack as Endrick laid the ball off for his unmarked team-mate to slot home. Vinicius was denied by Izwan shortly afterwards but he completed his hat-trick in the 21st minute when he was found unmarked in the six-yard box by Estevao’s low centre. Rayan had an effort disallowed for offside but Endrick added to Brazil’s lead in the 31st minute with a low effort from range which found the bottom right corner. Estevao also had a goal disallowed for a foul by Vinicius but the Chelsea winger added to Brazil’s tally just after the interval with a deflected shot from the edge of the box. Rayan rocked the crossbar soon after but the endeavour of the Bournemouth forward was rewarded in the 65th minute when he rounded substitute goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari to make it 6-0. Brazil rang the changes in the closing stages and Allan came off the bench to grab the seventh goal in the 74th minute. Speaking in the absence of the suspended Ancelotti, Brazil assistant Francesco Mauri lauded the commitment shown by Vinicius. “His attitude was fantastic. As we discussed before the match, you shouldn’t focus solely on the quality of the opponents, you just have to give your absolute best,” said the Italian. “He was a constant threat, providing great depth to our attack. He forced the opposition to double-mark him, which in turn allowed us to defend a bit more effectively.” Despite lengthy travel for the friendlies in Singapore, Mauri felt the effort had been worthwhile for the squad’s development. “Before the game, we told the players that it was really important to finish in the best way in these November FIFA dates because after this we have to wait until March for our next games, so it’s good to go home with a good feeling,” he said. item.title: Obasanjo begged Tinubu to make daughter Ogun governor, Fayose alleges
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has alleged that former President Olusegun Obasanjo sought President Bola Tinubu’s support for his daughter, Iyabo Obasanjo, to become governor of Ogun State but turned against the president after the request was unsuccessful. Fayose made the allegation on Monday during an interview on TVC while reacting to Obasanjo’s criticism of Tinubu’s administration and its economic reforms. The former governor claimed that Obasanjo approached former Ogun State Governor Olusegun Osoba to help persuade Tinubu to support his daughter’s governorship ambition. According to Fayose, Obasanjo’s decision to welcome Tinubu during the president’s visit to Ogun State in April 2026 was connected to the ambition. He said, “You know Iyabo Obasanjo, Obasanjo’s daughter. Obasanjo went to Chief Aremo Olusegun Osoba to help him beg Tinubu so that Iyabo Obasanjo would become governor of Ogun State. “That was the reason Obasanjo came to welcome President Tinubu. “The moment that did not work, Obasanjo simply remembered what Osoba wrote about him in his book and went to reply to him because what he wanted did not fly. “He will go and be begging behind the scene; when he does not get it, he will attack you.” Fayose also dismissed Obasanjo’s criticisms of the Tinubu administration, saying the former president had a history of finding fault with successive administrations and seeking attention. “We are overrating Obasanjo. That is the truth. It is a style. Nobody gets it done better than Obasanjo in life. If anybody wants to talk, it is either Obasanjo or nobody,” he said. “Obasanjo still wants attention, and he sees no good in anyone. That is the truth. If you look at Obasanjo, he criticised Yar’Adua and Jonathan. “In fact, he made himself an enemy of Jonathan. The moment he does not follow a day-to-day taking of permission from him, Obasanjo becomes uncomfortable.” Fayose further recalled that Obasanjo welcomed Tinubu to Ogun State in April 2026 for the inauguration of the Gateway International Cargo Airport, where he reportedly wore a matching outfit with the President and spoke favourably about him. Iyabo Obasanjo, a former senator and daughter of the ex-president, declared interest in the Ogun governorship race in February 2026 on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC). She later suspended her ambition after the party adopted Senator Solomon Adeola as its consensus candidate and defected to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). Fayose and Obasanjo have had a long-running political disagreement, with both men exchanging criticisms and allegations publicly over the years. item.title: Femi Ajasa: Onigbinde, Adeyanju, Do2dtun, others mourn late Vanguard Online Editor
item.description: Co-founder of BudgIT, Oluseun Onigbinde, Lawyer and human rights activist Deji Adeyanju, on-air personality Oladotun Kayode, popularly known as Do2dtun, and former presidential aide Bashir Ahmad are among public figures who have mourned the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s online editor, Olufemi Ajasa, who died on Sunday at the age of 44. The deceased’s death was announced by Vanguard Media Limited, which said he passed away at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital after a brief illness. In a statement, the newspaper’s editor, Eze Anaba, described Ajasa’s death as a major loss to the organisation and the journalism profession, noting his contributions to the growth of its digital operations and online journalism. Reacting to his death on Tuesday, Onigbinde said, “What a loss. This is a shocking exit. He always stayed in touch for data. May memories remain blessed.” Adeyanju, in a tribute shared on Facebook, described Ajasa as a longtime friend and brother, saying they shared a close relationship for nearly two decades. He wrote, “We shared a close friendship for nearly two decades, and losing such a trusted ally to the cold hands of death is truly heartbreaking. My heartfelt condolences go out to his family and the entire Vanguard Newspaper team for this irreparable loss. I will always hold onto the wonderful memories of our travels together and the countless ideas we exchanged. “The kindhearted never truly die—they live on in our hearts forever. May God comfort his loved ones, and may his gentle soul rest in perfect peace.” Do2dtun, who worked with Cool FM, also expressed grief over Ajasa’s death in a post on X, describing him as an exceptional journalist who maintained professionalism in his work. He said Ajasa refused to accept money to publish a blackmail-related story against him, adding that the journalist declined attempts to persuade him to run the report. “Femi Ajasa, your loss broke me. You are an amazing journalist, never biased and you were a professional to the core. You never used your pen for evil,” he wrote. Similarly, Bashir Ahmad, a former media aide to ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, said he had known Ajasa since 2016 and valued his professionalism, dedication to journalism and warmth towards people. In a post on X, Ahmad said the journalist’s death was a painful loss to his family, friends and the Nigerian media industry. “I have had the privilege of knowing and sharing a friendship with Mr. Ajasa since 2016. Over the years, I came to appreciate his professionalism, dedication to journalism and the warmth with which he related with people. His passing is a painful loss, not only to his family and loved ones but also to the Nigerian media industry, where he made meaningful contributions,” he wrote. item.title: Kano gov Yusuf invites marriage applicants after divorce from Kwankwaso’s daughter
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has invited women interested in marrying him to apply. The governor made the announcement on Monday while addressing pensioners at the Kano Government House. Yusuf said he had accepted the decision to remain with one wife for now but was open to marrying again. “Some days ago, I was being forced to become a being with one wife. I want to thank the good people of Kano who advised me to keep two wives, but for now, I have accepted one wife,” he said. He also confirmed that the divorce process had been initiated. “The governor has agreed to divorce her. Is it not the paper (notice of marriage dissolution)? The governor has issued that,” he said. He disclosed that he had directed the Commissioner for Information to place advertisements on radio stations and social media platforms to invite women interested in becoming his wives. The development comes after Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, daughter of former Kano State Governor and Yusuf’s former political godfather, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, filed for divorce at the Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, on Saturday. item.title: NDLEA busts transnational cocaine syndicate, arrests 8 members in Lagos, Kano
item.description: …Couriers on Nigeria-Niger-Libya-Europe Trip Excrete 634 Pellets in Custody By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said on Tuesday that its operatives have dismantled a transnational drug trafficking cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the desert via the Republic of Niger and Libya to Europe. The spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi, in a statement said, “As a result, eight members of the syndicate were arrested in well-coordinated intelligence-guided operations in Lagos and Kano. “All eight suspects who were nabbed between Friday 30th and Saturday 31st October 2026 were drug mules who had swallowed cocaine pellets, excreting a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilograms over several days in custody. Babafemi said, “The operation began on Friday, 30th October, when operatives of a Special Operations Unit of the Agency arrested the first suspect, 57-year-old Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos. “He later excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650 kg. “The next day, Saturday, 31st October, four more members of the cartel were stopped at the MM2 Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano. “They are Jackson Ahamefule, 43, who excreted 90 wraps weighing 1.950 kg; Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47, who excreted 85 wraps weighing 1.750kg; Marcel Nnabuike, 38, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.655kg; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.650kg. “The five mules arrested in Lagos excreted 399 wraps of cocaine weighing 8.655 kg in all. Intelligence from the Lagos operation showed that other members of the cartel had already travelled to Kano, where NDLEA officers at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport (MAKIA) were swiftly mobilised to intercept them at the arrival hall of the domestic terminal of the Kano airport. As a result, three other members of the syndicate, namely Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31, were identified and arrested. A body scan showed that all three had swallowed drugs, after which they were placed under excretion observation. Over the following days, Ifechukwu excreted 85 pellets of cocaine weighing 1.853 kg; Nwaorji expelled 80 pellets weighing 1.752 kg, while Chinaka excreted 70 pellets with a total weight of 1.535 kg. The suspects said they had planned to travel by road from Kano through the Republic of Niger to Libya, with Europe as the final destination for the drugs. item.title: PR cannot cover bad leadership, global experts warn
item.description: By John Alechenu Global public relations experts have warned governments and corporate organisations to stop using PR, propaganda or strategic messaging to hide leadership failures. Trust, they said, cannot be bought with publicity. It must be earned through integrity, accountability and actions that match promises. The warning came at a session on Ethical Leadership and Trust in a Divided World at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja, organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations. The panel featured the Alliance’s regional council chairs for Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Middle East and South Asia, and North America. It was moderated by Chimdi Neliaku, Chair of the NIPR Young Professionals Hub. For Europe, Global Alliance Vice President and Chair of its European Regional Council, Silvia Arto, said ethical leadership is shown in personal conduct, not public declarations. “To me, ethical leadership is lead by example. It’s walk the talk. It’s integrity,” she said, adding that integrity meant doing what was right even when nobody was watching. Trust, she warned, takes years to build but can be destroyed within seconds, particularly through social media. “Trust and ethical leadership, personal leadership, is built through actions, not declarations,” Arto said. She urged professionals to promote transparency, media literacy and dialogue while combating misinformation, propaganda and misuse of artificial intelligence. Citing the European Union’s AI Act, she called for human accountability and ethical guidelines for emerging technologies. Arto also invoked Yoruba wisdom, declaring: “Character is beauty.” From Asia-Pacific, Chair Jaffri Osman said effective leadership requires more than intellectual intelligence. Emotional and social intelligence matter just as much in building relationships across diverse communities. “Trust is built by leaders who understand beyond IQ. They have to understand EQ and SQ,” he said. Using Malaysia’s Sarawak region as an example of multicultural coexistence, Osman said professionals must understand local cultures, traditions and relationships to influence communities responsibly. “When we talk about influence, when we talk about communication, and when we talk about going ahead effectively in ethical communication, we must go respect,” he said. For Africa, Chair Ms Irene Lungu Chipili identified political messaging, democratic competition and misinformation as major threats to public confidence. She questioned whether citizens could trust messages from political parties and governments, arguing that the credibility of the messenger was as important as the information. item.title: Jonathan Warns Against Ethnic Rivalry, Political Intolerance Ahead Of General Elections
item.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned that the rising tide of political intolerance, thuggery, and deliberate stoking of ethnic rivalries pose a severe threat to Nigeria’s national existence and stability ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎Speaking at a high-level peace and security conference hosted by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja, Jonathan stressed that upcoming electoral cycles must not become catalysts for destructive division. He urged political leaders and citizens alike to prioritise national unity, democratic values, and responsible leadership over narrow partisan ambitions. Former President Goodluck Jonathan and others at a high-level peace and security conference in Abuja on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The former president also urged Nigerians to treat the upcoming 2027 general elections as a critical opportunity to choose credible leadership at both state and federal levels, prioritising competence over ambition. He warned that undermining national cohesion for political ambition poses a severe danger to the country’s existence. “Nothing could be more dangerous to our national existence than the deliberate encouragement of ethnic rivalry. We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and one country, both at the national level and at the state level”, he said. The post Jonathan Warns Against Ethnic Rivalry, Political Intolerance Ahead Of General Elections appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Reps hail unanimous approval of State Police by 36 assemblies
item.description: The House of Representatives has welcomed the approval by all 36 State Houses of Assembly of the proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Services. The House described the unanimous endorsement as a significant milestone in the constitutional amendment process, saying it represents 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures and exceeds the constitutional requirement of at least 24 State Houses of Assembly under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution. The House Spokesman, Rep. Akin Rotimi Jr., disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. According to the statement, the approval was confirmed by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, who said the bill had satisfied the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission. Ogunlana, in a statement issued on Monday, November 16, explained that the bill had earlier met the requirements for transmission but that the leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all states. He said: “The Bill had long satisfied all the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission as prescribed by the Constitution and the Acts Authentication Act Cap. A2, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, but the Leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay of transmission to allow for broader national consensus and engagement of all the States of the Federation.” The Clerk further confirmed that following the completion of the verification process by his office, the bill was ready for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. He described the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the National Assembly and the State Houses of Assembly, as well as between the executive arms of government at federal and state levels. The House of Representatives acknowledged the collective efforts of both chambers of the National Assembly and all 36 State Houses of Assembly in advancing the proposed constitutional reform. It particularly recognised the work of the House Committee on Constitution Review, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Benjamin Kalu. The House also commended the 36 state governors, speakers and members of the State Houses of Assembly, as well as other stakeholders, for their cooperation and commitment to the proposed reform of policing in Nigeria. It said the unanimous approval marked an important step towards strengthening the country’s security architecture, improving responses to local security challenges and advancing the establishment of State Police Services. The House added that the development would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to complete and transmit the remaining Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the State Houses of Assembly for consideration. item.title: NNPC confirms Lagos filling station fire contained
item.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has confirmed that a fire outbreak at an affiliated filling station along Ekoro-Ajasa Road, in Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State, has been contained. The company said preliminary information indicated that no fatalities or injuries were recorded in the incident, which occurred on Monday, November 16, 2026. NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja. The company acknowledged the fear and distress caused by the incident among residents, customers and businesses in the area, expressing sympathy with those whose properties or livelihoods might have been affected. NNPC commended the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and other emergency responders for containing the fire and preventing further damage. It said its Retail, Health, Safety and Environment teams, alongside the management of the affected filling station, were reviewing the cause of the incident. The company assured residents that the safety of customers, employees and neighbouring communities remained a priority. It added that it would support relevant authorities and the management of the affiliated filling station in addressing the incident, promising to provide further updates as verified information became available. The post NNPC confirms Lagos filling station fire contained appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, has said the United States is providing real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training to the Nigerian military to track and target terrorist leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to Reuters, Musa disclosed this on Monday during a briefing with journalists, saying the improved intelligence support had strengthened the military’s ability to identify and strike militant targets. The minister said Nigerian troops had killed several terrorist and bandit leaders in overnight operations in the Northwest and Northeast, adding that the military was conducting almost daily operations with improved intelligence. “We took out a lot of the bandit leaders and the terrorists themselves,” Musa said. He said Nigeria and the United States had continued to expand their security cooperation as the country battles Islamist insurgencies in the North-East, armed banditry in the North-West and kidnapping gangs across the country. Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting additional military helicopters from the United States and Italy to strengthen its operational capacity. On preparations for the 2027 general elections, the defence minister said security agencies were intensifying intelligence-led operations to prevent violence before, during and after the polls. He said authorities were also monitoring the use of Starlink satellite internet services, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones by militant groups, while working with US authorities to disrupt their financing networks. Musa further disclosed that Nigeria had reached a five-kilometre cross-border right-of-pursuit arrangement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue terrorists and bandits across border areas. The arrangement is aimed at restricting the movement of armed groups that exploit porous borders to escape security operations. The minister also warned that Islamic State Sahel was seeking to recruit criminal gangs in North-West Nigeria, raising concerns that largely profit-driven bandit groups could develop into ideologically driven insurgent organisations similar to the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP). According to him, militants and bandits have continued to exploit dense forests and porous borders with Niger and Benin to evade security forces after carrying out attacks. However, he said improved surveillance had strengthened the military’s ability to track armed groups through difficult terrain and restricted their freedom of movement. “We don’t want them to develop that capacity,” Musa said. “We’re blocking the logistics and taking them out from within Nigeria.” The post 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Obi highlights institutional reforms during Anambra tenure
item.description: Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has highlighted the institutional reforms undertaken by his administration, saying rebuilding the machinery of government was essential to achieving sustainable development. Obi disclosed this on Tuesday in the second instalment of his series, titled Nigerians, Go and Verify, published on his X handle. In the article, titled Building the Institutions of the State, the former governor explained that his administration prioritised strengthening government institutions under the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy, ANIDS, before embarking on broader development projects. He said his administration was guided by the principles of character, competence, capacity and compassion, adding that a development vision could not succeed without strong institutions to implement it. According to him, the physical and administrative structures of governance were in deplorable condition when he assumed office, making it necessary to rebuild institutions across the executive, legislature, judiciary, civil service and local government system. Restoring the seat of government Obi said his administration rebuilt, re-equipped and furnished the Government House in Awka after it was vandalised and burnt in 2004. He added that the Governor’s Lodge in Amawbia was rehabilitated, while a new Governor’s Lodge was constructed in Onitsha to strengthen executive presence and facilitate governance across the state’s major administrative and commercial centres. Strengthening the legislature and judiciary The former governor said his administration also rehabilitated the Anambra State House of Assembly Complex in Awka and provided vehicles to lawmakers to facilitate the discharge of their legislative responsibilities. He said the judiciary was equally strengthened through the provision of brand-new vehicles to High Court judges, which he described as the first of its kind in the state’s history. Obi also said vehicles were provided to magistrates for the first time since the creation of Anambra State. He explained that the interventions were aimed at improving mobility, strengthening the administration of justice and enabling judicial officers to perform their duties more effectively. Rebuilding the civil service On the civil service, Obi said many Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs, operated from scattered rented apartments before his administration, while civil servants lacked a centralised and decent working environment. He said the arrangement undermined administrative coordination, efficiency and the dignity of public service. To address the situation, he said his administration constructed the two-phase Chief Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex, comprising Blocks 1 and 2, to bring the MDAs together and provide civil servants with a more conducive working environment. item.title: FG introduces NIN-linked verification system for domestic air passengers
item.description: The Federal Government has introduced a biometric passenger verification system linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) for domestic air travel, in a move aimed at strengthening airport security and curbing identity fraud. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday after unveiling the Airport Passenger Verification System, known as V-PASS, at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. Keyamo said the system would make it mandatory for passengers on domestic flights to verify their identities using their NIN before boarding. He explained that the technology was designed to eliminate cases of passengers travelling with fake identities, as well as address touting and ticket racketeering at airports. According to him, the biometric identity verification system would enhance passenger processing, strengthen airport security and provide a faster and more seamless travel experience. The minister said the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement. He was accompanied at the unveiling by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Mrs Olubunmi Kuku; Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials. Keyamo said he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to give all airlines operating in the country until December 31 to integrate with the system. He clarified that the verification system was designed exclusively for domestic flights.
